language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: Q3 is largely pre-released, but the fuel assumption is likely a little light. JetBlue's 2026-09-10 update guided Q3 fuel at $3.96/gal off the 2026-09-04 Brent curve, with CASM ex-fuel raised to +6-8% for ATC and weather. Southwest's Q3 fuel came in at $3.92 against its own prior $3.70-3.75 assumption, so late-quarter fuel ran above earlier curves. JetBlue is unhedged, so an overshoot of $0.05-0.10/gal on ~220m gallons is about $11-22m, or $0.03-0.06 a share, against a -$0.53 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline reactions: +10.5% (Q2 2026), +1.21%, -6.89%, -11.86%, +6.65%, +2.7%, -25.71%. The reported quarter was pre-released in September, so this line has mostly been seen already.

findings.finding: The Q4 guide will be built on fuel far above anything JetBlue has guided this year. United guided Q4 at $4.80/gal (2026-10-21, Q4 EPS $0.50-1.50 vs ~$1.76-1.88 consensus), Southwest at ~$4.55/gal off the 2026-10-15 curve (Q4 EPS $0.55-0.80 vs $0.82 est.), and UBS models JetBlue at $4.85. JetBlue's Q3 guide was $3.96 and its July full-year guide assumed $3.49 with -2% to -5% operating margin, so the FY guide must be cut or suspended and Q4 will show a deep operating loss. JetBlue has no hedges.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 brought a weak outlook plus better-than-expected fuel recapture (nearly 50% recaptured), and the stock went +10.5%. The Q3 2025 print brought -11.86% and Q4 2024 brought -25.71%; the baseline does not say which line drove those. Peers' sharply below-consensus Q4 guides this month drew muted reactions (UAL -0.8% premarket, LUV +1% after hours).

findings.finding: The balance sheet is the line this print turns on, and the facts point both ways. (a) A senior creditor group holding the $2bn TrueBlue-backed 2031 notes and the ~$742m secured loan has hired PJT Partners and Akin Gump (WSJ/Bloomberg, 2026-10-24/25). The notes fell to 42 cents from ~80 earlier in October and the stock fell ~16% on 2026-10-26. (b) Against that, June 30 liquidity was $2.17bn of cash and investments plus an undrawn $600m revolver, against a $750m quarter-end minimum-liquidity covenant on the TrueBlue debt. UBS estimates ~$660m of H2 burn at $4.85 Q4 fuel and ~$1.6bn year-end liquidity, plus a possible $250m draw on a facility agreed in Q2. Scheduled debt repayments are only $236m for the rest of 2026 and $478m in 2027, and the company claims >$6bn of unencumbered assets. The 10:00 ET call is management's first chance to answer the creditor news. A Sept 30 liquidity figure well above the covenant reassures; an announced liability-management plan or adviser hire dilutes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July 2026 the 2031 notes fell to 84 cents and JetBlue scheduled a fixed-income investor meeting on liquidity (Bloomberg, 2026-07-23). The Q2 print that followed reacted +10.5%. That is one precedent where a liquidity scare before the print was followed by relief.

findings.finding: The print lands on a crowded short at the bottom of a capitulation. Short interest is reported above 30% of float (GuruFocus, 2026-10-22), from 96.2m shares at 4.1 days to cover on 2026-08-14. The stock is -45.4% over 20 sessions and -20.8% over 5, at its all-time low ($2.16 intraday on 2026-10-26). Put/call OI is 2.61. Any reassurance on liquidity or the creditor talks hits a short base of roughly 3-4 days of volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: +10.5% on the Q2 2026 print after a pre-print bond selloff and a run-in drawdown. No sourced history of squeezes on this name beyond that.

findings.finding: Demand and revenue are strong and were raised in September. Q3 RASM guidance went to +17-20% (midpoint 4 points above the prior guide), with 'no meaningful signs of demand elasticity' and 'early Q4 booking trends are encouraging'. Peers who reported since confirm record or double-digit revenue: UAL record $17.9bn, LUV record revenue and an EPS beat, ALK revenue +14%. That supports a Q4 RASM guide high enough to recapture part of the fuel increase, and Q2 recaptured nearly 50%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the release led with fuel recapture 'exceeding expectations', and the stock went +10.5%.

findings.finding: The JetForward long-range targets are at risk of withdrawal: $850-950m incremental EBIT by 2027, ~$1.2bn by 2028 and 2028 EPS of at least $1.00. Morgan Stanley warned in mid-October that prolonged fuel inflation threatens 2027 cost targets, and FCF is described as turning positive only around end-2027 into 2028 'if things go right'. A withdrawal or a push-out on the call would be a guidance negative.

findings.finding: China n-type rod polysilicon transaction prices (Silicon Industry Branch) rose from RMB 32,000/t in the week of 22 Jul to RMB 43,000/t in the week of 17-23 Sep (+34%), and held at 43,000 through the 21 Oct weekly print. So Q3 realised ASP should sit clearly above Q2's $4.04/kg (cash cost $4.57, total cost $5.95). Inventory marked to NRV at Q2-end prices (Q2 impairment $55.7m) is now being sold above its carrying value, which points to a smaller impairment and a narrower gross loss than Q2's $82.7m. Q4 opens at the higher price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: DQ has not paid for revenue or margin lines lately. Q4'25 (26 Feb 2026) beat on EPS and still fell 6.85% intraday on a revenue miss (https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1145858192). Q1'26 (29 Apr) fell 11.85% (sealed tape; the volume spike confirms the event day). Q2'26 (20 Aug) fell 14.6% on an EPS miss despite a sequential revenue rise (https://finviz.com/news/383985/daqo-new-energy-shares-tumble-after-q2-earnings-miss-and-weak-polysilicon-market).

findings.finding: Q3 sales volume is the swing line, and the evidence points both ways; net slightly positive. On 20 Aug management said shipments 'continued to pick up in the third quarter', that 'selling and shipping our product is really not an issue', and that it targets about 15% market share and lower inventory. Q2 sales were only 15,190 MT against 43,675 MT produced, and H1 was 87.1k produced against 19.7k sold. Against that, the industry's weekly reports show thin spot trade: the 28 Sep release was the first official price in almost two months, only 2-4 firms were transacting, and new orders were slow as of 21 Oct. A revenue bar of $77-140m implies roughly 16-29k MT at about $4.8/kg, so modest volume growth clears the low end. If Q3 sales stay well below the 40-45k MT production, the inventory and cash-burn worry continues.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume drove the last two prints. In Q1'26, sales of 4,482 MT against 38,167 MT in Q4'25 coincided with -11.85%. In Q2'26 volume recovered to 15,190 MT but ASP fell, and the stock dropped 14.6%.

findings.finding: Industry production cuts began in October: the Silicon Industry Branch expects utilization of about 35% from October, and a 30 Sep weekly projected October output of about 105k t, down 12.9% month on month. DQ's Q4 production guide is therefore likely to come in at the low end of, or below, what the FY guide implies (FY 160-180k MT less H1 87.1k and Q3 40-45k leaves about 28-53k MT for Q4). That supports price, but at about 57% of nameplate capacity already, a lower utilisation raises unit cost and idle-capacity charges, and the market has sold DQ's lower-volume quarters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Feb 2026 the FY26 production guide (140-170k MT) came with a revenue miss and the stock fell about 6.9%. No print in the history isolates a production-guide cut.

findings.finding: Montage Technology (688008.SS), the main DDR5 RCD/interface-chip competitor, pre-announced Q3 2026 on 2026-10-20: interconnect-chip revenue about RMB 2.047bn, +20.9% QoQ and +49.3% YoY, at 68.0-68.5% gross margin (up 0.6-1.1pt QoQ). Drivers it named: server-CPU demand from AI inference/agents, a large rise in DDR5 interface and companion-chip shipments, and a higher mix of Gen3/4/5 RCD. It expects demand to 'rise further' in Q4. Rambus guided Q3 product revenue to $110-116M, +14% QoQ and about +21% YoY at the midpoint (Q3 2025 product was $93.3M). Industry units were therefore not choked by DRAM supply in Q3, which supports a product print at or above the top of the guide and a firm Q4 product guide. Montage again grew faster than Rambus (+49% vs about +21% YoY), which feeds the share-loss bear case. The finding is sized net of that.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Product revenue and the guide are what this stock trades on. Q1 2026 missed on product (an OSAT issue) and fell -21.3% with the Baird downgrade. Q2 product came in at $99.2M, inside the $95-101M guide, with a Q3 product guide of +14% QoQ, and the stock fell -9.0%. The last product-led upside was Q2 2025 (+13.9%).

findings.finding: DRAM supply is expected to stay tight into 2027-2028. Per Reuters via TrendForce, 2026-10-08, Samsung and Micron both expect tight memory supply through 2028. TrendForce sees 2027 RDIMM bit supply growth of only 15-20%, below server-CPU growth. This is the exact mechanism of the April Baird downgrade: a volume-driven RCD model loses unit growth when RDIMM supply is constrained, with Baird modelling RDIMM units +20% in 2026 slowing to 12-15% in 2027. The risk sits on the Q4 guide and on 2027 commentary. A small offset: TrendForce reports systems shifting from 96/128GB to 32/64GB RDIMMs from 3Q26, which means more modules, and so more RCDs, per bit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Baird supply-constraint thesis came with the -21.3% reaction on 2026-04-28. In July the stock fell -9.0% on a beat as the forward commentary read 'in line'.

findings.finding: The Q2 2026 beat was royalty-led. Royalties were $84.2M against a $72-78M guide, while product was $99.2M, inside its $95-101M guide. A Q3 beat carried by royalties or contract revenue again would likely be treated the same way.

findings.finding: Currency tailwind into FQ4 (Jun-Aug 2026) is larger than in Q3. On the 2026-07-09 call management said June comps were +11.2% reported and +6.5% in constant currency, a 4.7-point FX lift against 3.8 points in Q3. The COP traded about 3,050-3,390 per USD in Jun-Aug 2026 against about 4,030-4,050 in late August 2025, roughly 25% stronger. The CRC traded about 449-454 against about 505 a year earlier. Colombia's Q3 reported net merchandise sales were +35.3% against +18.6% in constant currency. From Q4 FY25 net merchandise sales of $1,302.7M, total revenue lands near $1.49B (+12%). That is above MarketBeat's $1.46B bar (+9.7% implied) and below Benzinga's $1.51B. The same tailwind should carry into the September comps preview the company usually gives on the call (2026-10-27).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-07-08): revenue $1.48B beat consensus by about $60M while EPS $1.28 was reported as short of $1.32 (other sources say ahead of $1.23); the stock moved -0.45%. findings.finding: EPS is likely near or below the $1.27 bar even with the revenue tailwind. Q3 total other expense rose to a $10.5M net loss from $7.2M on additional FX conversion costs, and $44.1M of cash is trapped in Trinidad. Warehouse operating costs rose to 9.7% of revenue on Chile launch costs. Two clubs added pre-opening cost in the quarter: Ciudad Quesada opened in August and Montego Bay on 2026-10-01. Q4 FY25 base: operating income $52.75M (3.96% of revenue), other expense $5.59M, and a 32.0% tax rate against 27.4% FY26 year to date. At about $1.49B revenue, a 4.0-4.1% operating margin, about $8.5-10M other expense and a 28% tax rate, EPS comes to about $1.18-1.25, below MarketBeat's $1.27 and near Benzinga's $1.22. The tax normalisation is the one offset.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS shortfalls: Q4 FY25 $1.02 vs $1.08, -6.48%; Q3 FY26 EPS reported as short of $1.32 on a revenue beat, -0.45%. Q1 FY26 was reported by Benzinga as $1.29 vs $1.44 yet the stock rose 4.55%, so the EPS line is not a reliable driver either.

findings.finding: Colombian consumer demand outside vehicles slowed into the quarter. DANE retail sales were +5.3% real in July 2026 (the slowest since September 2024, below an 11.2% expectation) and +7.3% in August (below 8.5%), but only +1.9% excluding vehicles and motorcycles. PriceSmart's Colombia constant-currency comps were +18.9% in Q3, and Colombia is about 12% of sales, so a cc slowdown there would trim consolidated cc comps by a few tenths.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately observable. In Q3 Colombia cc comps of +18.9% coincided with a -0.45% reaction.

findings.finding: Q2 subscription revenue is guided to $264-268M, flat to down from Q1's actual $267.0M, and Q1 term-license revenue grew only +1% while management cited a term-duration headwind as customers assessed hardware/storage plans. On its own record Commvault guides conservatively: Q1 beat EPS $1.42 vs $1.16 and revenue $314.1M vs $310.5M. A beat of the $266M midpoint by ~1-2% is therefore the base case, but that is a quarter the company told the market to expect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold. Q1 FY27 (2026-07-28): EPS beat by $0.26 and revenue beat, stock -19.7% on the flat sequential subscription guide. 2026-01-27: -31.1%. 2025-10-28: -16.3%. Only 2026-04-28 (+10.8%) paid for a beat.

findings.finding: Rubrik, the closest listed cyber-resilience/backup peer, reported its July quarter on 2026-08-27, after Commvault last spoke. It exceeded every guided metric, raised every FY27 metric, and grew subscription ARR to $1.66B with net new subscription ARR +35% YoY and Cloud ARR +39%. That points to healthy category demand through Commvault's September quarter, especially for SaaS ARR (Commvault Q1 SaaS ARR $424M, +38%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history of CVLT reacting to Rubrik prints is in the baseline. CVLT's ARR/guide line drove the -19.7% in July and the +10.8% in April.

findings.finding: NetApp's July quarter (reported late Aug/early Sep 2026) showed revenue +30%, all-flash +47%, a raised FY27 guide and customers accelerating purchases as component costs rose. That is relevant to the on-prem/term-license line Commvault said was soft because customers were 'assessing hardware and storage plans'. A completed storage refresh would tend to unlock the attached backup term license in the September quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 term-license revenue +1% YoY was part of the guide disappointment that preceded the -19.7% move. There is no earlier history of CVLT reacting to the storage cycle in the baseline.

findings.finding: Into the print the stock is +9.5% over 5 sessions and +13.0% over 20, within 4% of its 52-week high and above the average analyst target ($160.7-163.5). Six target raises landed between 5 and 26 Oct, three of them from Neutral/Hold houses chasing the price (Cantor $132→$171, Jefferies $130→$170, Scotiabank $130→$160). This repeats the July set-up: Truist raised to $182 a week before, then a beat with a flat guide sold off -19.7%. A print that only meets the bar has room to fall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a 92% rally into July, a beat with a soft guide gave -19.7%. Of the last four prints, three fell by 16-31%.

findings.finding: Reuters reported on 2026-04-10 that Commvault is exploring a sale with Goldman Sachs after takeover interest, including an earlier offer from Thoma Bravo. No company statement or 8-K has closed the process since: EDGAR shows only an 8-K adding director David Morton, the CFO of Intapp, on 2026-09-22, with no mention of it, and an August report says no decision has been made. Companies often disclose a deal or an end to the review alongside results, so the print carries a two-sided tail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose ~13-17% on the day of the Reuters report (2026-04-10, to $88.52). There is no history of a print carrying deal news.
